text:
lucy (sre): quick postmortem follow-up: we keep seeing a repeating pattern - autoscaler backfill + KV cold-starts during failover windows. outcome yesterday: sustained throughput drop (~28%) and p99 spike for 40m. we should treat this as recurring and change our SLO strategy rather than one-off relaxations.

rafael (infra): agreed. short-term we patched node replacement cadence which helped, but root cause is the ramp profile. infra plan: smoother drain, staggered node onboarding, and an autoscaler safety cap. i'll own infra rollout. ETA 36h for phased deploy.

jamal (serving): serving side proposals: 1) cache pre-warm on failover + controlled KV refresh (avoid thundering), 2) soft cap on customer batch_size to prevent queueing spikes, 3) circuit-breaker to route to low-cost fallback model pool when region degradation > 10%. i'll take routing + cache work. ETA 72h for full testing.

tina (product): we need to decide how this impacts SLAs. several customers run bulk batch jobs nightly; if we change SLO semantics we must notify and offer temporary credits or throughput-guarantee add-on. i'll lead comms & SLA review.

lucy (sre): concrete SLO proposal to discuss in this thread before we change config: introduce a throughput-oriented SLO used only for burst windows and leave latency SLO for steady-state. example (draft):
```yaml
service: inference-api
slo:
  latency:
    p99_ms: 500
    window: 30d
  throughput:
    p50_req_per_sec: 120
    burst_window: 10m
    percentile: 95
error_budget_policy:
  dynamic_shift: true  # allow temporary error-budget reallocation during burst windows
  max_shift: 0.015
```
this allows us to isolate burst behavior and not automatically burn latency error budget for expected failovers during scale events.

rafael (infra): i like the dynamic_shift idea, but need guardrails. Suggest: max_shift applies per-customer and per-region, and we track shift_usage metric. i'll add metrics and dashboard panels for shift_usage and per-customer throughput SLO burn.

jamal (serving): will add metrics: kv_cache_warm_percent, batch_drop_rate, fallback_routing_fraction. also alerts: "throughput_slo_burn > 10% for 15m" and "batch_drop_rate > 1% for 5m".

tina (product): action items for rollout + customer impact:
- tina (product): SLA review + comms draft (due 24h)
- rafael (infra): autoscaler safety cap + shift_usage panels (due 36h)
- jamal (serving): cache prewarm + batch cap + alerts (due 72h)
- lucy (sre): SLO config PR & review with infra (due 12h)

deploy-bot: Incident #INC-2026-045 acknowledged - automation triggered node restart.

lucy (sre): i've opened a config PR placeholder: https://git.redwood/slo-config/pulls/420 - still drafting but comments welcome.

rafael (infra): logging note: we'll tag all replacement events with reason=autoscaler-backfill so we can query recurring incidents by tag.

jamal (serving): staging is green for cache pre-warm flow. pushing canary tomorrow. will post canary link.

tina (product): will prepare a short customer FAQ outlining "what changed", "why we introduced throughput SLO", and "options for guaranteed throughput".

lucy (sre): scheduling a backlog review in 4 days to evaluate whether throughput SLO becomes policy (permanent) or we revert to stricter latency SLAs after infra fixes. calendar: https://cal.link/4day-slo-bursts.

lucy (sre): final note: prefer making the throughput SLO opt-in for enterprise customers first, then evaluate telemetry across 30d before global roll. closing thread but will update with PR link and dashboards when available. :white_check_mark:
